thread:
OpsBot: ALERT: cluster-na-west-1 gpu-health: 99p token latency spike detected. Correlated signals: repeated PCIe AER events and NVLink link flaps on rack-14 nodes.

Maya: seeing the same in traces — 99p token latency jumped ~4x around 02:14 UTC. root signals point to AER/Xid bursts + NVLink retrain on r14n01-06.

Liam: can you paste the kernel logs / dmesg snippet?

Maya: sure — short extract:
```
[Feb 24 02:14:11] pcieport 0000:3e:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e1
[Feb 24 02:14:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI): 79, pid=4223, GPU=0000:3f:00.0
[Feb 24 02:14:12] nvlink: link_down reason=phy_failure, ln=1
[Feb 24 02:14:12] nvlink: retrain start
[Feb 24 02:14:13] nvlink: link_up
[Feb 24 02:14:14] NVRM: Xid (PCI): 43
```
These repeats happen ~every 20-40s for the six nodes.

Noah: quick checks: ECC error counters? `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,ERR` and `dmesg | grep -iA2 nvlink` — if ECC is ramping we should drain.

Maya: ECC counters are flat-ish, but AER counts and `pcie_aspm` show a flurry. Quick `nvidia-smi` from r14n03:
```
GPU 0: XXX (PCI:0000:3f:00:0)
Persistent ECC errors: 0
Xid Errors (last): 79, 43, 31
Link Status: NVLINK OK (retrain events: 8 last 5m)
```

Sophia: sounds like an interconnect/slot issue (riser / NVLink bridge) rather than DRAM ECC failure. Those retrains cause micro-pauses that blow up 99p latency for token streaming.

Rachel: capacity note — draining r14 (6 nodes) will free ~24 GPUs. NA-west has ~6% spare at the moment; if we drain 2 racks worth it's tight. We should plan a quick cold path: route high-latency tolerant jobs to eu-west or spin cloud spot gpus for the next 2 hours.

Liam: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes (`kubectl drain r14n01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`) 2) set autoscaler min buffer to +10% for na-west temporarily 3) enable fallback routing to eu-west/hosted for latency-insensitive traffic.

Maya: trying controlled drain on r14n03 now, will watch tail latencies.

DC-Tech: datacenter can be onsite to reseat riser + NVLink bridge at 03:30 UTC. If reseat doesn't help we can swap the riser / run with new bridge.

Maya: after cordon/drain r14n03 latency 99p dropped ~30% for the tenant seen in traces. r14n04 still flapping.

Noah: we should capture full GPU telemetry and a kernel crashdump for the vendor RMA. Sophia can you assemble the packet? include `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `pcie_aspm` state, and timestamps.

Sophia: on it — will also enable temporary alerting on NVLink retrain count > 3/min so we don't miss recurrence.

Rachel: cost ops — if we need to burst to cloud for 2 hours estimate ~ $2.5k. I'll pre-approve if the SLOs would otherwise be violated.

Liam: if reseat fixes it, we still want to replace the NVLink bridge and order a spare riser for that chassis. recurring retrain counts are a sign of flaky interconnect hardware.

OpsBot: Created ticket INF-9284 assigned to eng-infra, maintenance window requested 03:30-04:30 UTC.

DC-Tech: confirmed onsite 03:30. will reseat riser and test NVLink continuity.

Maya: follow-up plan: 
- drain r14n01-06 sequentially 
- reseat + test with synthetic NVLink stress (micro-bench) 
- if any node still retrains >3/min, mark for RMA and replace bridge/riser
- route non-critical traffic to eu-west / cloud while impacted racks are offline

Noah: action items assigned: Sophia -> telemetry + alert rule; Maya -> execute drains + run bench; DC-Tech -> reseat; Rachel -> approve burst if needed; Liam -> prepare RMA packet template.

Sophia: telemetry uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/triage/INF-9284/ (kernel logs, nvidia-smi snapshots, perf traces).

Rachel: approved cloud burst if SLOs impacted.

Maya: reseat in progress on r14n02-04 at 03:32 UTC. preliminary results: r14n02 stabilized after reseat, r14n04 still shows retrain events.

Liam: prepare RMA for r14n04 and r14n05. include last 24h AER/Xid timeline and dmesg.

DC-Tech: will swap riser on r14n04 at 04:00 UTC and report.

Maya: after swap r14n04 passed nvlink stress for 15m, no retrains seen. 99p latency back to baseline for impacted tenant.

Noah: good — treat as resolved for now. we'll keep alerting at lower threshold for 24h and if any node flaps again we'll proceed with full RMA.

Rachel: thanks team. please add incident notes to INF-9284 and tag billing for cloud burst.

Maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Liam: closing thread — leaving follow-up tasks in INF-9284.
